circuit_character: Managing the undulations and using them well is key
Overtaking is difficult so qualifying performance is important
Strong braking feel and brake combining are critical for lap time
Well-managed weight transfer is important for confidence
Load the car, feel the weight transfer, then turn
surface_notes: Be wary of bottoming when weaving or passing
Banking and camber are major tools for supporting the car through key corners
tyre_warmup_notes: LH tyres are predominantly used and carry high energy
Ensure the FR tyre is switched on before the first push lap
Avoid forcing the front tyres to grip before they are ready

notes: No explicit track limits sensor page was provided in this booklet
Use normal circuit limit judgement and measured lap validity data where available

T1.name: Tarzan
driving_focus: Brake straight with a flat wheel after the 100m board, aiming for 70m
Start to bleed the brake and turn in as the track starts to bank
Use the banking to support the car
The apex is further around the corner, looking for the end of the concrete barrier on the right
Avoid being too tight to the inside kerb because minimum speed will be too low
Use half of the exit kerb
Do not overuse the exit kerb because the car can bottom out
Modulate the brake bleed and combine well
Keep the FR on the edge of micro-locking
Use the slight gradient to keep the car loaded without forcing the fronts to grip

common_errors: Brake bleed too abrupt or too late
Too tight to the inside kerb causing low minimum speed
Forcing the front tyres rather than using the banking
FR lock or excessive micro-locking
Using too much exit kerb and bottoming

T2.name: Turn 2
driving_focus: Stay left with the kerb
Do not be enticed to point in too early for the right
Turn in just before the end of the kerb
Aim to get behind the apex kerb
Keep high on the right
The target line is about one third from the white line
Use this corner to open the banked Turn 3

common_errors: Pointing in too early for the right
Not getting behind the apex kerb
Dropping too low on the right
Compromising Turn 3 entry

T3.name: Banked Turn 3
driving_focus: Sustained G is key to keep the minimum speed up
Stay high on the banking but avoid crossing the white line
Be wary of opponents going low for a block pass
Do not fall too low because it is easy to lock the FL
Make sure to get off the brake
Load the car into the banking
Keep just below the white line
Be flat by the high-banking phase
Apply throttle quickly to build momentum, settle the car and get a strong exit
Use half of the exit kerb
The section between the two red lines has the most banking angle
Be cautious of a snap if going lower on the banking

common_errors: Falling too low on the banking
Locking the FL from staying on brake too long
Crossing the white line at the top of the banking
Late throttle application which loses momentum
Going lower on the banking and triggering a snap

T7.name: Turn 7
driving_focus: Arrive at the crest with a flat car
Use a small brake just after the kerb and pitch the car in
Turn at the access road
Do not turn in too late
Use the camber as the track drops away
Stay low and close to the white line
Look to pinch the start of the kerb
Avoid touching the inside kerb because it is very unsettling
If enough speed is carried, the car should just touch the exit kerb
Do not use too much exit kerb because you need to prepare for the following turn
Trust the car will be supported by the camber

common_errors: Arriving at the crest with an unsettled car
Turning in too late
Missing the support from the camber
Touching the inside kerb and unsettling the car
Using too much exit kerb and compromising the next turn

T8.name: Turn 8
driving_focus: Get behind the kerb on the left to open the entry
Be on the white line on entry
Turn in at the 50m board when the board is present
Be on power before the apex to settle the car
There is a slight bump so try to power through it
Carry the speed to the left
Follow the white line into the braking for T9
Drive the car with your feet
Use the free rotation from coming off the brake
Catch and settle the car by being fully on power by the apex

common_errors: Not getting behind the left kerb on entry
Turning in without opening the entry
Late throttle pickup before the apex
Lifting or hesitating over the bump
Not carrying enough speed left into the T9 braking approach

T9.name: Turn 9
driving_focus: Braking is tough because there is a constant radius
Use all the track and work to release the brake
Start to apply power at the apex
Let the car run out
Leave no more than one car width to the white line
Work hard to bring the car back over to prepare for T10
Attack the corner precisely
Good footwork is important
Slightly straightening the wheel for braking can aid braking efficiency

common_errors: Overdriving the corner
Poor brake release through the constant radius
Running too close to the white line on exit
Failing to bring the car back for T10
Leaving steering lock in during braking

T10.name: Turn 10
driving_focus: Braking is tough because the car is turning slightly
Use all the track and manage entry rotation with a good brake bleed-off
Leave a car width to the white line
Work to position the car pointing into the corner
Start to pick up power and keep vision up
Let the car run out to the exit kerb
Use a little exit kerb nearer the end if enough minimum speed is carried
The corner is mainly dictated by how T9 is negotiated
Do not rush the turn-in
The track widens a lot on exit
Rotate well early, get the power down and remove steering lock
Build a good exit heading into the chicane

common_errors: Rushing the turn-in
Poor positioning from T9
Not rotating early enough
Late power pickup
Keeping too much steering lock on exit

T11.name: Turn 11
driving_focus: Drive in the middle of the gantry to ensure good braking prep
Brake at the LED flag board on the left
Brake just after the start of the kerb
Keep a flat car while braking
Shave the brake and carry the speed in
Turn in before the end of the kerb
Use the inside kerb
Get in and low
Ensure the FL is on the kerb to keep the car hooked in
If the car can go easily flat between T11 and T12, the minimum speed through T11 is too low
In the wet, the orange sausage kerb can be used

common_errors: Poor approach position under the gantry
Over-slowing T11
Missing the inside kerb
Not getting the FL hooked on the kerb
Failing to carry enough speed in

T12.name: Turn 12
driving_focus: Arrive parallel to the white line with a flat car before braking
Brake at the LED digi flag board
Turn in before the kerb or white line
Turn in as the brake is released
Use the benefit of the camber
Use no more than half of the exit kerb
Avoid compromising the run down to T1
Use a controlled brake bleed-off to pitch the car into the camber
As the camber supports the car, add steering and pick up power
A good exit is critical

common_errors: Arriving not parallel to the white line
Braking with the car unsettled
Late turn-in after the kerb or white line
Not using the camber support
Using too much exit kerb and compromising the run to T1

intended_use: Use as context layer on top of delta analysis
Do not let advisory override measured data
Prefer advisory-based comments when a measured behaviour clearly conflicts with target technique
example_checks: If throttle pickup occurs materially after the stated target point, flag as late throttle relative to booklet
If gear channel differs from target gear at corner minimum speed, flag gear mismatch
If brake release is prolonged where the booklet asks for quick release, good bleed-off or brake shaving, flag weak rotation setup
If line position conflicts with a stated banking, camber or kerb-support target, flag line positioning loss
If steering scrub remains high on exit where the booklet asks for power down and steering lock removal, flag exit inefficiency
If T3 line is too low on the banking, flag snap risk and reduced banking support
If T11 to T12 is easily flat, flag likely under-commitment or low minimum speed at T11
